theThreeQuestionGate.a: hauska-map: the `cross-repo literal drift` job of .github/workflows/cross-repo-literal-drift.yml, two steps - `node scripts/check-cross-repo-literal-drift.mjs --selftest` (a temp-dir fixture run of the same predicate, both directions plus the refusal case) then `--side map --ldt-root ldt-main` against a sparse checkout of legacy-design-tools main. Same file, mirror flags, in legacy-design-tools. hauska-factory: two steps inside the existing `test` job (`check-public-literal-drift.mjs --selftest`, then `--map-root hauska-map-main --ldt-root ldt-p331-main`), because a public runner cannot read the private repo, so the defining side has to be the one that reaches out.

theThreeQuestionGate.q: What triggers it, and what happens when one repo changes and the other does not push?
theThreeQuestionGate.a: `pull_request` and `push` to main in both public repos, plus a nightly `schedule` (07:17Z in hauska-map, 07:23Z in legacy-design-tools) and workflow_dispatch; the factory's steps ride its existing `ci` workflow. A push to ONE repo does not re-run the other's CI - that is a fact about GitHub, not a gap in the check, and the schedule is what bounds it: the sibling's main is re-read on a clock, so a one-sided edit that no one pushed over is caught within a day. In the PR-time direction it is caught immediately, because each PR's job reads the sibling's main as it is at that moment - measured on these three PRs, where the sibling's main did not yet contain the branch.

Exit 1 (FAIL): the two values disagree; the message names the literal id, both values and both files, and the job fails. Exit 2 (REFUSE): a declaration could not be read where it is expected - renamed, moved, changed shape, or the sibling root/file unreadable; also fails the job, and is deliberately distinct from 1 because 'we cannot read it' is a different problem from 'they disagree'. Exit 3 is a usage error and fails too. Nothing exits 0 on doubt.

(1) A literal nobody added to the table - the table IS the enumeration; a new cross-repo copy is unwatched until a row exists, and the trigger to add one is any comment claiming a copy. (2) A literal DEFINED in the private hauska-factory: the public repos cannot read it, so those two literals are checked from the factory's CI against the public copies, and the direction 'a public repo changed and the factory did not' is watched only by the factory's copy of the cross-repo check for the literals the PUBLIC repos own - for the factory's two it is a named bypass, written in the script header. (3) A push to one repo does not re-run the other's CI - covered by the nightly schedule, and only from the day after. (4) Deleting or weakening the workflow step, or editing the check itself: it is a repo file, so whoever can change the literal can change the control - named in the header rather than left implicit. (5) The two copies of the check script are not compared with each other by a row YET (the sibling's main has no copy until both PRs merge, and a row that read a file the sibling lacks would REFUSE on every PR); they are committed byte-identical with the hash recorded, and the one-line row to add is handed over in leave_behind. (6) `union` members of a shape other than a string literal (map's `(string & {})` catch-all) are excluded from the comparison, and the exclusion is stated in the check.
